description:
Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: High (calibrated). BLOCKS THE EPIC PR (probabilistically).

Concrete failure: the full suite fails about 1 run in 5 on a quiet machine, on different tests each time. CI runs two matrix legs per push, so roughly a 36 percent chance at least one test job is red. Measured at 5220686 on Elixir 1.18.4/OTP 26.2.5: 5 clean sequential runs, 1 failure (Ancora.Scaffold.TemplatesTest, config template loads with the taught defaults).

Two independent root causes, both reproduced by the critical review:

(1) capture_io(:stderr, ...) inside async: true modules. ExUnit documents that concurrent captures of a named device see each other output. Reproducible at a fixed seed: mix test test/ancora/scaffold/templates_test.exs test/ancora/config_test.exs test/ancora/trailer_test.exs test/ancora/severity_test.exs --seed 4 fails about 1 run in 3, with TrailerTest [CONFIG] output landing inside TemplatesTest refute stderr matches [CONFIG].

(2) Temp paths are not unique across BEAM VMs. Per-test roots use System.unique_integer, whose counter restarts near zero in every VM, so two concurrent mix test runs collide and each cleanup deletes the other live fixtures. Ancora.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0 already exists for exactly this and is used nowhere in lib/ or test/.

Fix lands ON this branch before the PR. Tracked as a work order because it needs an implementer plus a cold verifier per the epic discipline.

Found by /ship-it preflight, critical review 2026-09-03, findings F2 and F3. Three reviewers plus orchestrator measurement agree.

comments.text:
Full detail from the /ship-it preflight.

Measurement (orchestrator, at 5220686, nothing else running on the machine):
- Elixir 1.18.4 / OTP 26.2.5, five consecutive full-suite runs: 0, 0, 0, 1 failure, 0. The failure was Ancora.Scaffold.TemplatesTest "config template loads with the taught defaults".
- Earlier runs of mine showed a higher rate (3 of 5 on OTP 26, 1 of 4 on OTP 28) but those were contaminated: nine reviewer agents were concurrently running mix against the same tree, which triggers root cause (2) directly. The 1-in-5 clean figure is the honest one. Recording the contamination because the inflated number is the more memorable one and it is wrong.
- Independent corroboration: the Distributed Systems reviewer ran the suite 12 times and saw 3 red runs hitting 6 distinct tests across 5 files; it also confirmed failures persist with --max-cases 1, which rules out ExUnit scheduling as the cause. Every failing test passes in isolation.

Deliverable, per consolidated findings F2 and F3:

F2 - Move Ancora.TrailerTest, Ancora.ConfigTest, Ancora.SeverityTest and Ancora.Scaffold.TemplatesTest to async: false, or split just their capture_io(:stderr, ...) tests into small sync modules. test/ancora/output_test.exs already demonstrates the pattern (it uses async: false at line 2 for this reason).

F3 - Route every temp path in test/support/ and test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs through Ancora.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0, and File.rm_rf! before File.mkdir_p! the way TmpGitRepo.create!/0 already does.

Related and worth folding in (consolidated F20, same area): there are four different ways this suite shells out to mix and only one sets MIX_QUIET, so Mix "Waiting for lock on the build directory" can land on asserted stdout. The known-flake fix from ancora-yzu.30 was applied only to the private helper inside spec_check_test.exs; Ancora.MixSubprocess (used by fresh_adopter_test) does not set it. Consolidating on one helper in Ancora.TestCase with MIX_QUIET plus the stderr wrapper, and giving each subprocess its own MIX_BUILD_PATH, removes the whole class.

Verification:
- The seed-4 command above green across repeated runs.
- Full suite run 20 times on BOTH matrix legs (1.18.4/OTP 26.2.5 and 1.19.5/OTP 28.3.1) with zero failures. The bar is repetition, not a single green run - a single run proves nothing at a 20 percent rate.
- Do not weaken any assertion to achieve green.

Allowed touches: test/**
Out of scope: lib/** behavior changes; weakening assertions.

Consolidated report: /Users/mz/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-03/ancora-yzu-spec-anchored-successor/20260903-052243-consolidated.md

IMPLEMENTED
Session: rdx-impl-1
Log: /Users/mz/.local/state/agentic-runs/ancora/ancora-rdx/codex-rdx-impl-1/log

Commit: 4dc1b395cacdb8db34b49053bd47d18749fc2cc6
Files touched: test/ancora/config_test.exs, test/ancora/scaffold/fresh_adopter_test.exs, test/ancora/scaffold/templates_test.exs, test/ancora/severity_test.exs, test/ancora/trailer_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_validate_test.exs, test/support/ancora_case.exs, test/support/mix_subprocess.exs (deleted), test/support/tmp_git_repo.exs
Tests added: none; the existing Mix.Tasks.Spec.CheckTest subprocess capture positive control now exercises Ancora.TestCase.run_mix_subprocess/2
Spec acknowledgment: Spec-Ack: derived/growth=info (the new test-to-Ancora.TempName binding is mechanical and does not change the contract)
Verification tier: change-scoped — mix test --stale; test/ancora/config_test.exs, test/ancora/scaffold/fresh_adopter_test.exs, test/ancora/scaffold/templates_test.exs, test/ancora/severity_test.exs, test/ancora/trailer_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs, and test/mix/tasks/spec_validate_test.exs; mix spec.check --base 5220686; full-system proof deferred to the merge gate / PR CI
Final-tier runs: 1
Seed-4 repro: before = failed on repetition 5 with Ancora.Scaffold.TemplatesTest config stderr cross-talk / after = 5 of 5 green, 39 tests and 0 failures each
Full-suite repetition: run 1 = 3 properties, 331 tests, 0 failures; run 2 = 3 properties, 331 tests, 0 failures; run 3 = 3 properties, 331 tests, 0 failures; run 4 = 3 properties, 331 tests, 0 failures; run 5 = 3 properties, 331 tests, 0 failures

Summary: The four stderr-capturing modules now run synchronously, and all shared test temp roots use cross-VM suffixes with pre-cleanup. Every nested Mix call now goes through one stderr-preserving helper with MIX_QUIET and a private build path. No epic lessons block was present, and every ticket rule was checked against the final diff.

ORCHESTRATOR MECHANICAL REMEDY — Spec-Ack trailer removed (commit message only; tree byte-identical).
Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

The implementation is good and its proof is real (seed-4 repro failed before the fix on repetition 5, 5/5 green after; five consecutive full-suite runs at 331 tests + 3 properties, 0 failures). One defect required remedy before merge-back.

Defect: the worker added a `Spec-Ack: derived/growth=info` trailer for what it expected to be a new test-to-Ancora.TempName binding. The trailer is CODE-scoped, not binding-scoped, so it downgraded EVERY derived/growth finding in the branch range — including the ancora.review warning that is blocker 1 (ancora-ayj). Measured with the trailer in place:
  mix spec.check --base ecc5e24  ->  39 findings (error=0 warning=0 info=39)  ->  spec.check result=pass
That is a false pass. It would have shipped a green CI over an unfixed blocker, which is the exact failure mode ancora-ayj's description warns against.

The trailer was also unnecessary. With ANCORA_SHOW_INFO=1 against the ticket base, this diff produces exactly 7 findings, all derived/unresolved_calls, and ZERO derived/growth. No TempName binding finding exists.

Remedy applied by the orchestrator (deterministic, message-only):
  git commit --amend  dropping the single trailer line.
  Proof the tree is untouched: old tree 9d813f9b71ad5a4d053aacd1aa813d1af528cf9d == new tree 9d813f9b71ad5a4d053aacd1aa813d1af528cf9d. Commit 4dc1b39 -> cfc229f.

Execution proof after the remedy:
- mix spec.check --base 5220686  ->  spec.check result=pass  (ticket base, unchanged)
- mix spec.check --base ecc5e24  ->  spec.check result=fail tier=branch errors=0 warnings=1  (main; correctly red again, because blocker 1 is genuinely still unfixed and belongs to ancora-ayj)

Counted as a mechanical-remedy remedy (1 of 2), not a bounce against the implementer's substantive work. Cold verification of the diff follows before merge-back.

VERIFY: PASS (agent verify-rdx, opus, cold; relayed verbatim in substance by the orchestrator — cross-worktree verify, verdict delivered by teammate message in two parts)
Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

Mechanical checks:
- Files touched: 10; outside test/**: 0. No lib/** path in the diff.

Assertion-weakening audit (the primary risk on a flake ticket):
- 380 test/property declarations at base and 380 at head; sorted name lists diff empty. Nothing deleted, renamed, or skipped; zero @tag :skip in the tree. refute count 101 at base, 101 at head.
- config_test / trailer_test / severity_test / templates_test: single-line async change each; no assertion touched.
- fresh_adopter_test: three MixSubprocess.run calls rerouted; assertions byte-identical.
- spec_check_test: thirteen run_mix calls rerouted, private run_mix/1 deleted; every assertion unchanged.
- spec_validate_test: four bare {stdout, N} = System.cmd matches became assert %{stdout: stdout, status: N} = run_mix_subprocess(...). Equal strictness (a bare match already raises MatchError); accounts for the entire +4 assert delta.
- refute stderr =~ "[CONFIG]" in TemplatesTest: present and unchanged, byte-identical to base with surrounding context.
- stderr capture preserved in the consolidated helper (same sh wrapper redirecting to $ANCORA_STDERR_FILE, still File.read!). Proven non-vacuous by spec_check_test.exs:170, a POSITIVE stderr assertion that passes.
- MIX_QUIET positive control at spec_check_test.exs:128 exercises the surviving helper and asserts exact list equality, so dropping MIX_QUIET makes it two elements and fails.

Root-cause fixes:
- (a) All five files in test/ that call capture_io(:stderr now declare async: false (output_test and the second severity_test module were already false at base). Grep for :standard_error across test/ and lib/ found no other capture site. Nothing missed.
- (b) TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0 (OS pid + 12 hex from strong_rand_bytes) backs the per-test root, the subprocess wrapper dir, and TmpGitRepo.create!/0, each with File.rm_rf! before File.mkdir_p!. One surviving System.unique_integer at git_test.exs:43 already carries System.pid(), so it is cross-VM safe and out of the ticket's named scope.

Re-runs:
- spec.check --base 5220686: spec.check result=pass (exit 0, findings=7, error=0 warning=0 info=7)
- diff-touched test files (all seven): 57 tests, 0 failures
- seed-4 repro x5: 39 tests, 0 failures (five times)
- full suite x5, sequential, quiet machine: 3 properties, 331 tests, 0 failures (five times, ~32s each)
- Trailer removal independently confirmed: commit message is the single subject line, zero Spec-Ack occurrences, tree hash 9d813f9b71ad5a4d053aacd1aa813d1af528cf9d as claimed.
- spec.check --base ecc5e24: spec.check result=fail tier=branch errors=0 warnings=1 with the ancora.review derived/growth warning printed in full. The blocker is VISIBLE, not masked.

Verdict: PASS. Gaps: none.

Beyond the brief, and the reason this verdict is worth trusting: the verifier built a throwaway worktree at base 5220686 and ran the seed-4 repro 30 times there, reproducing the failure once on repetition 7 with exactly the ticket's signature (refute stderr =~ "[CONFIG]" / left: "[CONFIG] .spec/config.yml is not valid YAML (malformed yaml); using defaults"). It then ran the same command 50 times on the fixed tree with 0 failures, and ran two full suites CONCURRENTLY at head (which directly triggers root cause 2) with both green. It also corrected the ticket's own rate estimate: on this box the repro is ~1 in 30, not 1 in 3, which makes the mandated 5 runs statistically thin — hence the extra 50.

Notes (advisory, non-blocking):
- seed_build_path! does a File.cp_r! of _build/test (4.5 MB) per subprocess call, ~30 calls per full run (~135 MB copied). Suite still finishes in 32s; it is why the touched-file run takes 25s, and it scales with _build.
- Private build dirs land at _build/ancora-mix-<suffix> and are cleaned at the end of run_mix_subprocess rather than in on_exit, so a mid-flight crash could leave one behind. Zero leftovers observed across 60+ runs; theoretical.
- Four previously-unquieted callers gain MIX_QUIET for the first time. Verified this cannot make their refutes vacuous: ancora never writes through Mix.shell() anywhere in lib/ (grep returns nothing), it prints via IO.puts, so MIX_QUIET suppresses only Mix's own diagnostics; each refute is paired with a positive assert in the same test.
- Follow-up for a different ticket: lib/ancora/review/spec_diff.ex:32 builds a temp root from a bare System.unique_integer with no pid component — the same cross-VM collision class, in lib/ and therefore out of scope here. Already carried in the consolidated review as F21/F41.

elixir-test-critic record follows (required: this diff makes assertional test edits).

TEST_CRITIC: PASS (agent critic-rdx, elixir-test-critic; relayed by the orchestrator)
Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

Blocking findings: none

Assertion strength: equal-or-stronger on all five conversions in spec_validate_test.exs (four were bare matches, one already carried assert). Every status pinned to a literal integer: status: 1 at lines 11 and 22, status: 0 at 23 and 39, status: 1 at 43 and 66. The map-pattern-matches-a-subset concern does not bite: System.cmd/2 returns exactly {output, status} and both elements are accounted for in the new form, so nothing asserted positionally became unasserted. Three ways it got STRONGER: bare matches now raise an ExUnit assertion failure instead of MatchError; the failure report prints the whole result map including stderr, which the old tuple could not carry; and stderr, which previously leaked to the parent's fd 2 and vanished into the runner's terminal, is now captured.

async:false judgement: right instrument, accounting exact. `grep -rn 'capture_io(:stderr' test/` returns nine sites across five modules — output_test.exs:370,437 (both already async: false at base, confirmed via git show 5220686:) plus trailer_test x4, severity_test:125, config_test:135, templates_test:43, precisely the four the diff converts. Every remaining named-device capture now sits in a sync module and none sits there gratuitously.
The critic did NOT trust the macro — it loaded all seven affected files under ExUnit.start(autorun: false) and read :sys.get_state(ExUnit.Server): async = [FreshAdopterTest, Spec.CheckTest, Spec.ValidateTest], sync = [ConfigTest, TemplatesTest, Severity.InfoEnvTest, SeverityTest, TrailerTest]. The three `use Ancora.TestCase` callers passing no options stayed async, so the Keyword.get(unquote(options), :async, true) default behaves. Serialization cost measured: all four sync modules run 39 tests in 0.4s; the expensive subprocess modules stay async.
Solving it without capturing a named device would require production changes (IO.puts(:stderr, ...) hardcodes the atom at trailer.ex:115, config.ex:504, output.ex:110); the critic judged that a bad trade for a flake fix, since stderr is ancora's diagnostic channel by contract and the strong end-to-end proof already lives in an async subprocess test reading a real file.

Consolidated helper risk (run_mix_subprocess/2, ancora_case.exs:99-135, 30 call sites):
- Separation preserved: wrapper does 2>"$ANCORA_STDERR_FILE" before exec, child's fd 2 to file, fd 1 stays the pipe, System.cmd defaults stderr_to_stdout: false. spec_check_test.exs:168 is the standing proof and would go red if the redirect were dropped.
- MIX_QUIET suppression scope verified by grep, not assumption: `grep -rn "Mix\.shell\|Mix\.raise\|IO\.puts\|IO\.write\|IO\.warn" lib/` returns ZERO Mix.shell() calls (only Mix.raise and IO.puts), and Mix.Shell.Quiet stubs only info/1 while error/1 defdelegates to Mix.Shell.IO. So MIX_QUIET silences Mix chatter and leaves ancora's output and Mix's error reporting intact.
- One vacuous-pass path exists and PREDATES this diff: spec_check_test.exs:63-65 asserts status != 0 then refutes stdout, with no positive stdout assertion, so an empty-string helper would pass it. Same shape existed in the deleted run_mix, so not a regression. Every other subprocess refute is guarded by a paired positive assertion on the same stream (:170 by stderr =~ "[CONFIG]"; :213 by List.last(lines(stdout)) =~ ..., which raises FunctionClauseError on nil =~ if stdout were empty; spec_validate_test.exs:29 by the checked-counts assertion).
- Cleanup is NOT on the failure path: File.read!/rm_rf! calls sit after System.cmd with no on_exit, so a raise or ExUnit timeout leaks the wrapper dir and _build/ancora-mix-<suffix>. Same shape as the deleted helper, so not a regression, and it cannot corrupt assertions — nothing in lib/ or test/ walks _build, and the leading rm_rf! on a fresh cross_vm_suffix makes collision impossible regardless. Clean runs leave nothing (git status empty, no _build/ancora-mix-* after a run).
- MIX_ENV=test is correctly paired with seed_build_path! (which copies Mix.Project.build_path() = _build/test); no config/ dir exists, so no env-dependent behavior shifts under the assertions.

Positive control: spec_check_test.exs:128-138 runs `mix run -e 'Mix.shell().info("Waiting for lock on the build directory"); IO.puts(~s({"ok":true}))'` through the surviving helper and asserts lines(result.stdout) == [~s|{"ok":true}|] by EXACT list equality. Two-sided: deleting MIX_QUIET makes the lock line land on stdout (two elements, fail); silencing the process wholesale drops the {"ok":true} line (fail from the other side).

AUDIT: APPROVE (auto — selective audit)
Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

Reasoning: every selective-audit condition holds. Cold verifier verdict PASS with zero Gaps. Mechanical scope clean: 10 files touched, 0 outside the ticket's `test/**` Allowed glob, 0 matching Out-of-Scope, no intent-level concerns (no lib/** behavior change). Spec gate carries a passing verdict against the ticket base (spec.check result=pass, findings=7, error=0 warning=0). The assertional-test-edit condition was NOT skipped: this diff converts four bare matches to asserts in spec_validate_test.exs, so an elixir-test-critic ran and returned TEST_CRITIC: PASS with no blocking findings, posted above. Seam disclosure is complete — the consolidated run_mix_subprocess/2 helper's risk paths are enumerated (stdout/stderr separation proven by a standing positive assertion, MIX_QUIET scope verified by grep against lib/, the single vacuous-pass path identified as pre-existing and unchanged, cleanup-off-failure-path identified as pre-existing and proven unable to corrupt assertions). No disclosed seam substitutes production wiring; the helper shells out to the real mix binary and reads a real stderr file.

The must-coverage clause is n/a for this diff: it is test-infrastructure only and introduces no requirements. The passing spec gate against the ticket base is the mechanical evidence that no existing requirement regressed.

Mechanical-remedy count this ticket: 1/2 (the orchestrator's commit-message trailer removal, tree proven byte-identical). Bounces against the implementer's substantive work: 0.

Proceeding to merge-back into the epic branch.

title: Fix the two test-isolation races that make the suite nondeterministically red
